title.zh: 卷一百〇七 列傳第五十七: 玄宗諸子
title.raw: 卷一百〇七 列傳第五十七: 玄宗諸子 Volume 111 Biographies 57: Xuanzong's Sons

sentences.zh: 玄宗三十子：元獻楊皇后生肅宗，劉華妃生奉天皇帝琮、靖恭太子琬、儀王璲，趙麗妃生廢太子瑛，錢妃生棣王琰，皇甫德儀生鄂王瑤，劉才人生光王琚，貞順武皇后生夏悼王一、懷哀王敏、壽王瑁、盛王琦，高婕妤生潁王璬、郭順儀生永王璘，柳婕妤生延王玢，鐘美人生濟王環，盧美人生信王瑝，閻才人生義王玭，王美人生陳王珪，陳美人生豐王珙，鄭才人生恆王瑱，武賢儀生涼王璿，汴哀王璥，余七王早夭。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong had thirty sons: Empress Yuanxian Yang bore Suzong; Consort Liu Hua bore the Emperor of Fengtian Cong, the Jinggong Crown Prince Wan, and Prince of Ceremonies Lin; Consort Zhao Li bore the deposed Crown Prince Ying; Consort Qian bore Prince of Di Yan; Huangfu Deyi bore Prince of E Yao; Lady Liu bore Prince of Guang Ju; Empress Zhenshun Wu bore the Xiaosi Prince Yi, the Huai'ai Prince Min, Prince of Shou Mao, and Prince of Sheng Qi; Lady Gao bore Prince of Ying Jing; Lady Guo Shun bore Prince of Yong Lin; Lady Liu bore Prince of Yan Bin; Lady Zhong bore Prince of Ji Huan; Lady Lu bore Prince of Xin Huang; Lady Yan bore Prince of Yi Mi; Lady Wang bore Prince of Chen Gui; Lady Chen bore Prince of Feng Gong; Lady Zheng bore Prince of Heng Zhen; Lady Wu Xian bore Prince of Liang Xuan and the Bian'ai Prince Jin; the remaining seven princes died young.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had thirty sons. Empress Yuanxian of the Yang clan bore Emperor Suzong. Consort Liu Hua bore the future Emperor of Fengtian (Cong), the Jinggong Crown Prince (Wan), and the Prince of Ceremonies (Lin). Consort Zhao Li bore the deposed Crown Prince Ying. Consort Qian bore the Prince of Di (Yan). Huangfu Deyi bore the Prince of E (Yao). Lady Liu bore the Prince of Guang (Ju). Empress Zhenshun of the Wu clan bore the Xiaosi Prince (named Yi), the Huai'ai Prince Min, the Prince of Shou (Mao), and the Prince of Sheng (Qi). Lady Gao bore the Prince of Ying (Jing). Lady Guo Shun bore the Prince of Yong (Lin). Lady Liu bore the Prince of Yan (Bin). Lady Zhong bore the Prince of Ji (Huan). Lady Lu bore the Prince of Xin (Huang). Lady Yan bore the Prince of Yi (Mi). Lady Wang bore the Prince of Chen (Gui). Lady Chen bore the Prince of Feng (Gong). Lady Zheng bore the Prince of Heng (Zhen). Lady Wu Xian bore the Prince of Liang (Xuan) and the Bian'ai Prince (Jin). Seven other princes died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 廢太子瑛，玄宗第二子也，本名嗣謙。

translations.literal: The deposed Crown Prince Ying was Emperor Xuanzong's second son; his original name was Siqian.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed Crown Prince Ying was Xuanzong's second son. His birth name was Siqian.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年九月，封真定郡王。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Jingyun, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhending commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of the Jingyun era (710), he was created Prince of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 先天元年八月，進封郢王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Xiantian, he was advanced to Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of the Xiantian era (712), he was promoted to Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 開元三年正月，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Kaiyuan, he was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Kaiyuan (715), he was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，加元服。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, he received the cap of manhood.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year (719), he underwent the coming-of-age ceremony.

sentences.zh: 其年，玄宗又令太子詣國子學行齒胄之禮，仍敕右散騎常侍褚無量升筵講論，學官及文武百官節級加賜。

translations.literal: That year, Xuanzong also ordered the crown prince to go to the Directorate of Education to perform the ceremony of donning armor by age rank, and further commanded the Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Chu Wuliang to ascend the dais and lecture; academic officials and civil and military officials all received graded additional gifts.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, Xuanzong had the crown prince visit the Imperial University to perform the ceremonial donning of armor according to seniority. He also ordered Chu Wuliang, Right Regular Attendant of the Imperial Cavalry, to take the lectern and discourse on the classics. The academic officers and all civil and military officials received additional gifts scaled by rank.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改名鴻，納妃薛氏，禮畢，曲赦京城之內，侍講潘肅等並加級改職，中書令蕭嵩親迎，特封徐國公。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, his name was changed to Hong; he took Lady Xue as consort. When the rites were completed, a partial amnesty was declared within the capital. Lecturers such as Pan Su were all promoted in rank and reassigned in office. Chief Minister Xiao Song personally went to meet the bride, and he was specially enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (725), his name was changed to Hong. After he took Lady Xue of the Xue clan as his consort and the wedding rites were concluded, a partial amnesty was proclaimed within the capital. Lecturers including Pan Su were promoted and given new posts. Chief Minister Xiao Song went in person to welcome the bride, and the prince was specially created Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 二十五年七月，改名瑛。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year, his name was changed to Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year (737), his name was changed to Ying.

sentences.zh: 瑛母趙麗妃，本伎人，有才貌，善歌舞，玄宗在潞州得幸。

translations.literal: Ying's mother, Consort Zhao Li, was originally a performer. She had talent and beauty and excelled at song and dance. Xuanzong favored her while he was at Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's mother, Consort Zhao Li, had been a performing artist. Gifted and beautiful, she was skilled in song and dance. Xuanzong took her to his bed while he was still in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 及景雲升儲之後，其父元禮、兄常奴擢為京職，開元初皆至大官。

translations.literal: After Jingyun, when he was raised as heir apparent, her father Yuanli and brother Changnu were promoted to capital offices; in the early Kaiyuan period they all reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: After he was named heir apparent in the Jingyun era, her father Yuanli and brother Changnu were appointed to posts in the capital. By the early Kaiyuan years they had all risen to high office.

sentences.zh: 及武惠妃寵幸，麗妃恩乃漸弛。

translations.literal: When Consort Wu Huifei gained favor, Consort Li's grace gradually slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Once Consort Wu Huifei won the emperor's favor, Consort Zhao Li's standing gradually waned.

sentences.zh: 時鄂王瑤母皇甫德儀、光王琚母劉才人，皆玄宗在臨淄邸以容色見顧，出子朗秀而母加愛焉。

translations.literal: At that time, Prince of E Yao's mother Huangfu Deyi and Prince of Guang Ju's mother Lady Liu were both noticed for their looks while Xuanzong was at his Linzi residence. Their sons were bright and handsome, and their mothers received added affection.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, Huangfu Deyi, mother of the Prince of E (Yao), and Lady Liu, mother of the Prince of Guang (Ju), had both caught Xuanzong's eye for their beauty while he was still prince at Linzi. Their sons were handsome and accomplished, and the mothers were all the more cherished for it.

sentences.zh: 及惠妃承恩，鄂、光之母亦漸疏薄，惠妃之子壽王瑁，鐘愛非諸子所比。

translations.literal: When Huifei received favor, the mothers of E and Guang also gradually grew distant and slighted. Huifei's son, Prince of Shou Mao, was cherished in a way unmatched among the other sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Consort Wu came into favor, the mothers of the Princes of E and Guang were likewise gradually pushed aside. Her son, the Prince of Shou (Mao), was doted upon as none of the other princes were.

sentences.zh: 瑛於內第與鄂、光王等自謂母氏失職，嘗有怨望。

translations.literal: Ying, at the inner residence with the Princes of E and Guang and others, considered that their mothers had lost their positions and at times harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Within the inner quarters, Ying and the Princes of E and Guang and the like felt that their mothers had fallen from favor, and they sometimes gave voice to their grievances.

sentences.zh: 惠妃女咸宜公主出降於楊洄，洄希惠妃之旨，規利於己，日求其短，譖於惠妃。

translations.literal: Huifei's daughter, Princess Xianyi, was married to Yang Hui. Hui hoped to please Huifei's wishes and scheme profit for himself. Day by day he sought their faults and slandered them to Huifei.
translations.idiomatic: Huifei's daughter, Princess Xianyi, had married Yang Hui. Eager to curry favor with Huifei and advance his own interests, Hui daily hunted for their failings and whispered accusations against them to the consort.

sentences.zh: 妃泣訴於玄宗，以太子結黨，將害於妾母子，亦指斥於至尊。

translations.literal: The consort wept and complained to Xuanzong that the crown prince was forming factions and would harm her and her son, and also spoke reproachfully of the sovereign himself.
translations.idiomatic: The consort wept before Xuanzong and accused the crown prince of forming factions and plotting harm against her and her son, even casting aspersions on the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 玄宗惑其言，震怒，謀於宰相，意將廢黜。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was swayed by her words, flew into a rage, and consulted with the chief ministers, intending to depose him.
translations.idiomatic: Taken in by her words, Xuanzong was furious. He took counsel with his chief ministers and resolved to depose the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 中書張九齡奏曰：「陛下纂嗣鴻業，將三十年，太子已下，常不離深宮，日受聖訓。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling memorialized: "Your Majesty has inherited the great enterprise and will soon have reigned thirty years. From the crown prince downward, they have constantly not left the deep palace and daily received your sagely instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling submitted: "Your Majesty has inherited the great enterprise and will soon complete thirty years on the throne. From the crown prince on down, your sons have scarcely left the inner palace and have daily received your instruction.

sentences.zh: 今天下之人，皆慶陛下享國日久，子孫蕃育，不聞有過，陛下奈何以一日之間廢棄三子？

translations.literal: Now all under heaven rejoice that Your Majesty has long enjoyed the realm and that your sons and grandsons flourish. No fault has been heard of them. How can Your Majesty in a single day cast aside three sons?
translations.idiomatic: All the realm rejoices that you have long held the throne and that your sons and grandsons flourish. No wrongdoing has been reported against them. How can Your Majesty, in a single day, cast aside three sons?

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下思之。

translations.literal: I humbly beg Your Majesty to reflect on this.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly urge Your Majesty to reconsider.

sentences.zh: 且太子國本，難於動搖。

translations.literal: Moreover, the crown prince is the root of the state and hard to dislodge.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the crown prince is the foundation of the state and must not be lightly moved.

sentences.zh: 昔晉獻公惑寵嬖之言，太子申生憂死，國乃大亂。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Xian of Jin was misled by the words of a favored concubine; Crown Prince Shensheng died in grief, and the state fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, Duke Xian of Jin was swayed by a favored woman's words. Crown Prince Shensheng died in despair, and the state was thrown into chaos.

sentences.zh: 漢武威加六合，受江充巫蠱之事，將禍及太子，遂至城中流血。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han's martial might extended over the six directions, yet he accepted the witchcraft affair of Jiang Chong; disaster nearly reached the crown prince, and blood flowed in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han, whose martial might reached the four seas, was taken in by Jiang Chong's witchcraft scandal. Calamity nearly engulfed the crown prince, and blood ran in the streets of the capital.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝有賢子為太子，容賈後之譖，以至喪亡。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui of Jin had a worthy son as crown prince, yet he tolerated Empress Jia's slanders, until he was lost and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui of Jin had a worthy son as crown prince, yet he tolerated Empress Jia's slanders until both throne and heir were lost.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝取寵婦之言，廢太子勇而立晉王廣，遂失天下。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui took the words of a favored woman, deposed Crown Prince Yong and installed Prince of Jin Guang, and thereby lost the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui heeded a favored woman's counsel, deposed Crown Prince Yong, and installed Prince Guang of Jin in his place—and in the end lost the empire.

sentences.zh: 由此而論之，不可不慎。

translations.literal: Judging from these examples, one cannot but be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Judging from these precedents, the matter cannot be treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 今太子既長無過，二王又賢，臣待罪左右，敢不詳悉。

translations.literal: Now the crown prince has grown up without fault, and the two princes are likewise worthy. Your servant, holding office at Your Majesty's side, dares not fail to set this forth in full.
translations.idiomatic: Today the crown prince has come of age without fault, and the two princes are likewise worthy. Your servant, who stands in attendance at Your Majesty's side, dares not withhold the full truth.

sentences.zh: 」玄宗默然，事且寢。

translations.literal: " Xuanzong was silent, and the matter for the time lay dormant.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanzong said nothing, and for the time being the matter was set aside.

sentences.zh: 其年，駕幸西京，以李林甫代張九齡為中書令，希惠妃之旨，托意於中貴人，揚壽王瑁之美，惠妃深德之。

translations.literal: That year, the imperial carriage visited the Western Capital. Li Linfu replaced Zhang Jiuling as chief minister. Currying Huifei's wishes, he conveyed his intent through the inner eunuchs and praised the virtues of Prince of Shou Mao. Huifei was deeply grateful.
translations.idiomatic: That year the court moved to the Western Capital. Li Linfu replaced Zhang Jiuling as chief minister. Eager to please Huifei, he worked through the palace eunuchs to praise the Prince of Shou (Mao), and the consort was deeply obliged to him.

sentences.zh: 二十五年四月，楊洄又構於惠妃，言瑛兄弟三人與太子妃兄駙馬薛鏽常構異謀。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-fifth year, Yang Hui again framed matters before Huifei, saying that Ying and his two brothers, together with the crown prince's consort's elder brother, the imperial son-in-law Xue Xiu, were constantly plotting strange designs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-fifth year (737), Yang Hui again pressed his case before Huifei, alleging that Ying and his two brothers, together with Xue Xiu—the crown prince's consort's elder brother and an imperial son-in-law—were constantly plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 玄宗遽召宰相籌之，林甫曰：「此蓋陛下家事，臣不合參知。

translations.literal: Xuanzong hastily summoned the chief ministers to deliberate. Linfu said: "This is surely Your Majesty's family affair; your servant ought not to take part in knowing it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong at once summoned the chief ministers to deliberate. Li Linfu said, "This is surely a matter of Your Majesty's household. It is not for your servant to intervene.

sentences.zh: 」玄宗意乃決矣。

translations.literal: " Then Xuanzong's mind was decided.
translations.idiomatic: " With that, Xuanzong's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 使中官宣詔於宮中，並廢為庶人，鏽配流，俄賜死於城東驛。

translations.literal: He sent inner eunuchs to proclaim the edict within the palace. All were deposed to commoner status. Xiu was sentenced to exile, and soon was granted death at the eastern relay station outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: He sent palace eunuchs to proclaim the edict within the palace. All three princes were reduced to commoners. Xue Xiu was sentenced to exile and soon ordered to take his own life at the relay station east of the city.

sentences.zh: 天下之人不見其過，鹹惜之。

translations.literal: People throughout the realm had not seen their faults and all lamented them.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the realm, no one could see what crime they had committed, and all mourned their fate.

sentences.zh: 其年，武惠妃數見三庶人為崇，怖而成疾，巫者祈請彌月，不痊而殞。

translations.literal: That year, Consort Wu Huifei repeatedly saw the three deposed men as apparitions. Terrified, she fell ill. Sorcerers prayed for a full month, but she did not recover and died.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, Consort Wu Huifei repeatedly dreamed that the three deposed princes haunted her as spirits. Stricken with terror, she fell ill. Sorcerers prayed for her for a full month, but she did not recover and died.

sentences.zh: 瑛有六男：儼、伸、倩、俅、備、亻敬。

translations.literal: Ying had six sons: Yan, Shen, Qian, Qiu, Bei, and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had six sons: Yan, Shen, Qian, Qiu, Bei, and Jing.

sentences.zh: 慶王琮先無子，瑛得罪後，玄宗遣鞫之。

translations.literal: Prince of Qing Cong had earlier had no sons. After Ying's offense, Xuanzong sent men to investigate and select one.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qing (Cong) had had no sons. After Ying's disgrace, Xuanzong ordered an inquiry to select an heir for him.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，儼為新平郡王、光祿卿同正員，伸為平原郡王、宗正卿同正員，俅為嗣慶王。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao period, Yan was made Prince of Xinping commandery and Acting Regular Commissioner of the Imperial Household; Shen was made Prince of Pingyuan commandery and Acting Regular Director of the Imperial Clan; Qiu was made heir to the Prince of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era, Yan was created Prince of Xinping and given the acting rank of Commissioner of the Imperial Household; Shen was created Prince of Pingyuan and given the acting rank of Director of the Imperial Clan; and Qiu was named heir to the Prince of Qing.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，詔雪瑤、瑛、琚之罪，贈瑛為皇太子，瑤、琚復贈為王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, an edict cleared the crimes of Yao, Ying, and Ju. Ying was posthumously given the title of crown prince; Yao and Ju were again posthumously given princely titles.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying (762), an edict cleared the crimes of Yao, Ying, and Ju. Ying was posthumously restored as crown prince; Yao and Ju were again granted their princely titles.

sentences.zh: 棣王琰，玄宗第四子也，初名嗣真。

translations.literal: Prince of Di Yan was Emperor Xuanzong's fourth son; his original name was Sizhen.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Di (Yan) was Xuanzong's fourth son. His birth name was Sizhen.

sentences.zh: 開元二年十二月，封為鄫王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of Kaiyuan (714), he was created Prince of Zeng.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月，改封棣王，仍改名洽。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twelfth year, he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Di and his name was also changed to Qia.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twelfth year (724), he was re-created Prince of Di and his name was changed to Qia.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遙領太原牧、太原已北諸軍節度大使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he held in title the governorship of Taiyuan and the military commissioner post for all armies north of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (727), he was given nominal appointment as governor of Taiyuan and military commissioner for all forces north of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，加太子太傅，余如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, he was given the additional title of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year (734), he was additionally appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; his other titles were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，改名琰。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, his name was changed to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year (736), his name was changed to Yan.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年六月，遙領兼武威郡都督、河西隴右經略節度大使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Tianbao, he held in title the concurrent posts of governor of Wuwei commandery and military commissioner for the Hexi and Longyou frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of Tianbao (742), he was given nominal concurrent appointment as governor of Wuwei and military commissioner for the Hexi and Longyou frontier.

sentences.zh: 先是，琰妃韋氏有過，琰怒之，不敢奏聞，乃斥於別室。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yan's consort, the Lady Wei, had committed an offense. Yan was angry with her but dared not report it. He confined her to a separate chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yan's consort, Lady Wei of the Wei clan, had given offense. Yan was furious but dared not report it to the throne. He shut her away in a separate apartment.

sentences.zh: 寵二孺人，孺人又不相協。

translations.literal: He favored two secondary consorts, and the secondary consorts also did not get along.
translations.idiomatic: He took two junior consorts to his bed, and the two could not abide each other.

sentences.zh: 至十一載，孺人乃密求巫者，書符置於琰履中以求媚。

translations.literal: By the eleventh year of the era, a secondary consort secretly sought a sorcerer to write a talisman and place it in Yan's shoe to win his favor.
translations.idiomatic: By the eleventh year of Tianbao (752), one of the junior consorts secretly engaged a sorcerer to inscribe a charm and slip it into Yan's shoe in hopes of winning his affection.

sentences.zh: 琰與監院中官有隙，中官聞其事，密奏於玄宗，雲琰厭魅聖躬。

translations.literal: Yan had a rift with a supervising eunuch of the residence. The eunuch heard of the affair and secretly memorialized Xuanzong that Yan was using sorcery to curse the sacred person of the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had fallen out with a eunuch who supervised his household. When the eunuch learned of the charm, he secretly reported to Xuanzong that Yan was practicing witchcraft against the emperor's person.

sentences.zh: 玄宗使人掩其履而獲之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong sent men to search his shoes and recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong sent men to search Yan's shoes and found the charm.

sentences.zh: 玄宗大怒，引琰詰責之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was greatly enraged and summoned Yan to interrogate and reproach him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong was furious. He summoned Yan and interrogated him under accusation.

sentences.zh: 琰頓首謝曰：「臣之罪合死矣，請一言以就鼎鑊。

translations.literal: Yan kowtowed and apologized: "Your servant's crime deserves death. I beg one word before I go to the cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Yan kowtowed and said, "Your servant's crime deserves death. Allow me one word before I face the executioner's cauldron.

sentences.zh: 然臣與新婦，情義絕者，二年於茲，臣有二孺人，又皆爭長。

translations.literal: Yet between your servant and the new consort, affection has been severed for two years now. Your servant has two secondary consorts, and both contend for precedence.
translations.idiomatic: Yet between your servant and his principal consort, all affection has been dead these two years. I have two junior consorts, and both vie for dominance.

sentences.zh: 臣實不知有符，恐此三人所為也。

translations.literal: Your servant truly did not know of the talisman; I fear these three women did it.
translations.idiomatic: I truly knew nothing of the charm. I fear it was the work of these three women.

sentences.zh: 惟三哥辯其罪人。

translations.literal: I beg only that the third brother identify the guilty party.
translations.idiomatic: I ask only that the third brother be allowed to identify the culprit.

sentences.zh: 」及推問之，竟孺人也。

translations.literal: " When the matter was pressed in inquiry, in the end it was a secondary consort.
translations.idiomatic: " When the matter was investigated, the culprit proved to be one of the junior consorts.

sentences.zh: 玄宗猶疑琰知情，怒未解，太子已下皆為請，命囚於鷹狗坊中，絕朝請，憂懼而死。

translations.literal: Xuanzong still suspected Yan had known of it; his anger was not assuaged. From the crown prince downward, all pleaded on his behalf. He was ordered imprisoned in the Hawk and Hound Ward, denied attendance at court, and died of anxiety and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong still suspected that Yan had known of the plot, and his anger did not abate. From the crown prince on down, all pleaded for him, but the emperor ordered Yan imprisoned in the Hawk and Hound Ward, barred from court attendance. He died of grief and fear.

sentences.zh: 琰妃即少師韋滔女，無子，琰死後，妃得還其父。

translations.literal: Yan's consort was the daughter of Junior Preceptor Wei Tao. She had no sons. After Yan's death, the consort was able to return to her father.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's consort was the daughter of Junior Preceptor Wei Tao. She bore no sons. After Yan's death, she was permitted to return to her father's house.

sentences.zh: 琰男女繁衍，至五十五人。

translations.literal: Yan's sons and daughters multiplied until they reached fifty-five persons.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's sons and daughters multiplied until they numbered fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 天寶中封為王者三人：僎為汝南郡王、秘書監同正員，僑為宜都王、衛尉卿同正員，雋為濟南王、光祿卿同正員。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao period, three were enfeoffed as princes: Fu as Prince of Runan commandery and Acting Regular Director of the Secretariat; Qiao as Prince of Yidu and Acting Regular Minister of the Guard; Jun as Prince of Jinan and Acting Regular Commissioner of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era, three of his sons were created princes: Fu as Prince of Runan with the acting rank of Director of the Secretariat; Qiao as Prince of Yidu with the acting rank of Minister of the Guard; and Jun as Prince of Jinan with the acting rank of Commissioner of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年五月，代宗即位，舍琰罪，贈其王位。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Baoying, when Daizong took the throne, Yan's crime was set aside and his princely title was posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Baoying (762), when Emperor Daizong ascended the throne, Yan's crime was pardoned and his princely title was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 鄂王瑤，玄宗第五子也，初名嗣初。

translations.literal: Prince of E Yao was Emperor Xuanzong's fifth son; his original name was Sichu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of E (Yao) was Xuanzong's fifth son. His birth name was Sichu.

sentences.zh: 開元二年五月，封為鄂王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of E.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Kaiyuan (714), he was created Prince of E.

sentences.zh: 十二年，改名涓，遙領幽州都督、河北道節度大使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, his name was changed to Juan; he held in title the governorship of Youzhou and the military commissioner post for the Hebei circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (724), his name was changed to Juan. He was given nominal appointment as governor of Youzhou and military commissioner for the Hebei circuit.

sentences.zh: 二十一年四月，加太子太保，兼幽州都督，余如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-first year, he was given the additional title of Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent and concurrent governorship of Youzhou; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-first year (733), he was additionally appointed Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent with concurrent governorship of Youzhou; his other titles were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，改名瑤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, his name was changed to Yao.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year (735), his name was changed to Yao.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，得罪廢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he offended and was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year (737), he fell from favor and was deposed.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年五月追復。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Baoying, he was posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Baoying (762), his title was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 靖恭太子琬，玄宗第六子也，初名嗣玄。

translations.literal: The Jinggong Crown Prince Wan was Emperor Xuanzong's sixth son; his original name was Sixuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinggong Crown Prince (Wan) was Xuanzong's sixth son. His birth name was Sixuan.

sentences.zh: 開元二年三月，封為甄王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Kaiyuan (714), he was created Prince of Zhen.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月，改名滉，封為榮王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twelfth year, his name was changed to Huang and he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twelfth year (724), his name was changed to Huang and he was re-created Prince of Rong.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授京兆牧，又遙領隴右節度大使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was appointed governor of Jingzhao and also held in title the military commissioner post for Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (727), he was appointed governor of the capital district and given nominal command as military commissioner for Longyou.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加開府儀同三司，余如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was given the additional title of Grand Master with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year (735), he was additionally appointed Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank; his other titles were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，改名琬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, his name was changed to Wan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year (737), his name was changed to Wan.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年六月，授單於大都護。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Tianbao, he was appointed Grand Protector of Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of Tianbao (742), he was appointed Grand Protector of Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 十四年十一月，安祿山反於范陽，其月制以琬為征討元帥，高仙芝為副，令仙芝征河、隴兵募屯於陜郡以禦之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourteenth year, An Lushan rebelled at Fanyang. That month an edict made Wan supreme commander for the campaign of suppression and Gao Xianzhi his deputy, ordering Xianzhi to levy troops from the He and Long circuits and encamp at Shaan commandery to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourteenth year (755), An Lushan rebelled at Fanyang. That same month an edict named Wan supreme commander for the punitive campaign, with Gao Xianzhi as his deputy, and ordered Xianzhi to levy troops from the He and Long circuits and encamp at Shaan to meet the rebels.

sentences.zh: 數日，琬薨。

translations.literal: Within several days, Wan died.
translations.idiomatic: Within days, Wan died.

sentences.zh: 琬素有雅稱，風格秀整，時士庶冀琬有所成功，忽然殂謝，遠近鹹失望焉。

translations.literal: Wan had long borne a refined reputation; his bearing was elegant and composed. At the time, scholars and commoners alike hoped Wan would achieve success. When he suddenly died, near and far all were disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Wan had long enjoyed a reputation for refinement; his bearing was elegant and dignified. Scholars and commoners alike had hoped he would distinguish himself. When he died so suddenly, people throughout the realm were deeply disappointed.

sentences.zh: 贈靖恭太子，葬於見子西原。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title Jinggong Crown Prince and buried on the western plain at Jianzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as the Jinggong Crown Prince and buried on the western plain at Jianzi.

sentences.zh: 琬諸子尤繁衍，男女五十八人。

translations.literal: Wan's sons were especially prolific; sons and daughters numbered fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Wan's offspring were especially numerous: fifty-eight sons and daughters in all.

sentences.zh: 天寶中封為郡王者二：俯為濟陰王、太仆卿同正員，偕為北平王、國子祭酒同正員。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao period, two were enfeoffed as commandery princes: Fu as Prince of Jiyin and Acting Regular Minister of the Stud; Xie as Prince of Beiping and Acting Regular Rector of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era, two of his sons were created princes: Fu as Prince of Jiyin with the acting rank of Minister of the Stud; and Xie as Prince of Beiping with the acting rank of Rector of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 夏悼王一，玄宗第九子也。

translations.literal: The Xiaosi Prince Yi was Emperor Xuanzong's ninth son.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiaosi Prince (named Yi) was Xuanzong's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 母貞順皇后為惠妃，見寵。

translations.literal: His mother, Empress Zhenshun, was Huifei and received favor.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, later Empress Zhenshun, was then Consort Wu Huifei, who was in high favor.

sentences.zh: 一生而美秀，上鐘愛無比，名之為一。

translations.literal: From birth he was beautiful and graceful. The sovereign cherished him beyond compare and named him Yi.
translations.idiomatic: From birth he was beautiful and accomplished. The emperor doted on him as on no other child and gave him the name Yi.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，孩孺而薨，玄宗追封謚。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan, he died still an infant. Xuanzong posthumously enfeoffed him and gave a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan (717), he died in infancy. Xuanzong posthumously enfeoffed him and granted a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 時車駕在東都，葬於城南龍門東岑，欲宮中舉目見之。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial carriage was at the Eastern Capital. He was buried on the eastern slope of Longmen south of the city, so that the palace might see it at a glance.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then at the Eastern Capital. He was buried on the eastern slope of Longmen, south of the city, so that the palace could look out and see the tomb.

sentences.zh: 儀王璲，玄宗第十二子也，初名濰。

translations.literal: Prince of Ceremonies Lin was Emperor Xuanzong's twelfth son; his original name was Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ceremonies (Lin) was Xuanzong's twelfth son. His birth name was Wei.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年五月，封為儀王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan (725), he was created Prince of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授河南牧。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was appointed governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (727), he was appointed governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加開府儀同三司，兼河南牧，其年改名璲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was given the additional title of Grand Master with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank and concurrent governorship of Henan. That year his name was changed to Lin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year (735), he was additionally appointed Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank, with concurrent governorship of Henan. That year his name was changed to Lin.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年二月薨，廢朝三日，贈太傅。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Yongtai, he died. Court was suspended for three days. He was posthumously given the title Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Yongtai (765), he died. Court mourning was observed for three days. He was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 天寶中有子封王者二人：侁為鐘陵郡王、光祿卿同正員，僆為廣陵王、國子祭酒同正員。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao period, two sons were enfeoffed as princes: Shen as Prince of Zhongling commandery and Acting Regular Commissioner of the Imperial Household; Mian as Prince of Guangling and Acting Regular Rector of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era, two of his sons were created princes: Shen as Prince of Zhongling with the acting rank of Commissioner of the Imperial Household; and Mian as Prince of Guangling with the acting rank of Rector of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 潁王璬，玄宗第十三子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Ying Jing was Emperor Xuanzong's thirteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ying (Jing) was Xuanzong's thirteenth son.

sentences.zh: 讀書有文詞。

translations.literal: In reading he had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was learned and skilled in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 初名澐。

translations.literal: His original name was Yun.
translations.idiomatic: His birth name was Yun.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年，封潁王。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan (725), he was created Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遙領安東都護、平盧軍節度大使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he held in title the posts of Protector-General of Andong and military commissioner of the Pinglu army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (727), he was given nominal appointment as Protector-General of Andong and military commissioner of the Pinglu army.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加開府儀同三司，改名璬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was given the additional title of Grand Master with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank, and his name was changed to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year (735), he was additionally appointed Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank, and his name was changed to Jing.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，除蜀郡大都督、劍南節度大使，楊國忠為之副。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he was appointed Grand Protector of Shujun and military commissioner of Jiannan, with Yang Guozhong as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Jing was appointed Grand Protector of Shujun and military commissioner of Jiannan, with Yang Guozhong as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 玄宗幸蜀，令御史大夫魏方進充置頓使，先移牒至蜀，托以潁王之籓，令設儲供。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong went to Shu, he ordered Censor-in-Chief Wei Fangjin to serve as provisioning commissioner. Fangjin first sent a dispatch to Shu, citing the Prince of Ying's fief, and ordered stores and supplies to be prepared.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong fled to Shu, he appointed Censor-in-Chief Wei Fangjin provisioning commissioner. Fangjin sent word ahead to Shu in the name of the Prince of Ying's fief and ordered provisions laid in.

sentences.zh: 玄宗至馬嵬，方進被殺，乃令璬先赴本郡，以蜀郡長史崔圓為副。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong reached Mawei, Fangjin was killed. He then ordered Jing to go first to his own commandery and made Cui Yuan, senior administrator of Shujun, his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: At Mawei, Fangjin was killed. Xuanzong then ordered Jing to proceed at once to his own commandery and appointed Cui Yuan, senior administrator of Shujun, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 璬性儉率，將渡綿州江，登舟見彩緣席為藉者，顧曰：「此可以為寢處，奈何踐之？

translations.literal: Jing's nature was frugal and plain. About to cross the river at Mianzhou, he boarded a boat and saw colored-bordered mats used as bedding. He looked back and said: "These could serve as a place to sleep—how can they be trampled?
translations.idiomatic: Jing was frugal by nature. As he was about to cross the river at Mianzhou, he boarded a boat and saw brocade-edged mats laid out as bedding. He turned and said, "These could serve as a bed—how can they be trodden underfoot?

sentences.zh: 」命撤去。

translations.literal: " He ordered them removed.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered them taken away.

sentences.zh: 璬初奉命之籓，卒遽不遑受節，綿州司馬史賁進說曰：「王，帝子也，且為節度大使。

translations.literal: When Jing first received orders to go to his fief, in the sudden haste he had no time to receive his credentials. The Mianzhou aide Shi Benjin advised: "Your Highness is the emperor's son and moreover a military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing first set out for his fief, the rush was so great that he had no time to receive his commissioner's credentials. The Mianzhou aide Shi Benjin urged him: "Your Highness is the emperor's son and a military commissioner besides.

sentences.zh: 今之籓而不持節，單騎徑進，人何所贍？

translations.literal: Now you go to your fief without holding credentials and advance alone on horseback—what will people look to for authority?
translations.idiomatic: To go to one's fief without credentials, riding ahead alone—what authority will that convey to the people?

sentences.zh: 請建大槊，蒙之油囊，為旌節狀，先驅道路，足以威眾。

translations.literal: I beg you to erect a great spear, cover it with an oiled bag in the shape of banners and credentials, and send it ahead on the road—that will be enough to awe the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Let us raise a great spear, drape it with an oiled bag in the shape of banners and credentials, and send it ahead on the road—that alone will be enough to overawe the crowd.

sentences.zh: 」璬笑曰：「但為真王，何用假旌節乎？

translations.literal: " Jing laughed and said: "If one is a true prince, what need is there for false banners and credentials?
translations.idiomatic: " Jing laughed and said, "If one is a true prince, what need is there for counterfeit banners and credentials?

sentences.zh: 」將至成都，崔圓迓之，拜於馬前，璬不止之，圓頗怒。

translations.literal: " As he was about to reach Chengdu, Cui Yuan went out to meet him and bowed before his horse. Jing did not stop him, and Yuan was quite angry.
translations.idiomatic: " As he neared Chengdu, Cui Yuan came out to meet him and bowed before his horse. Jing did not bid him rise, and Yuan was deeply offended.

sentences.zh: 玄宗至，璬視事兩月，人甚安之。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong arrived, Jing attended to affairs for two months, and the people were greatly at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuanzong arrived, Jing governed for two months, and the people were greatly reassured.

sentences.zh: 為圓所奏，罷居內宅。

translations.literal: He was memorialized against by Yuan and dismissed to dwell in the inner residence.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan memorialized against him, and he was removed to dwell in the inner palace quarters.

sentences.zh: 後令宣慰肅宗於彭原，遂從歸京師。

translations.literal: Later he was ordered to go as envoy of consolation to Suzong at Pengyuan, and then followed him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was later sent as envoy of consolation to Suzong at Pengyuan and thereafter returned with him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 建中四年薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of the Jianzhong era, 783.

sentences.zh: 年六十六，輟朝三日。

translations.literal: He was sixty-six years old. Court was suspended for three days.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-six. Court mourning was observed for three days.

sentences.zh: 子伸，天寶中封滎陽郡王，授衛尉卿同正員。

translations.literal: His son Shen, in the Tianbao period, was enfeoffed as Prince of Xingyang commandery and given the acting rank of Minister of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen was created Prince of Xingyang during the Tianbao era and given the acting rank of Minister of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 懷哀王敏，玄宗第十五子也。

translations.literal: The Huai'ai Prince Min was Emperor Xuanzong's fifteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai'ai Prince Min was Xuanzong's fifteenth son.

sentences.zh: 幼而豐秀，以母惠妃之寵，玄宗特加顧念。

translations.literal: In youth he was plump and handsome. Because of his mother Huifei's favor, Xuanzong paid him special regard.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was plump and handsome. Because his mother, Consort Wu Huifei, was in favor, Xuanzong doted on him all the more.

sentences.zh: 才晬，開元八年二月薨，追封謚，權窆於景龍觀。

translations.literal: He had just reached his first birthday when in the second month of the eighth year of Kaiyuan he died. He was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title and provisionally buried at the Jinglong Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He had scarcely reached his first birthday when he died in the second month of the eighth year of Kaiyuan, 720. He was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title and provisionally interred at the Jinglong Abbey.

sentences.zh: 天寶十三載，改葬京城南，以祔其母敬陵也。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao, he was reburied south of the capital to be placed beside his mother's Jing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao, 754, he was reburied south of the capital so that he might be placed beside his mother in the Jing Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 永王璘，玄宗第十六子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Yong Lin was Emperor Xuanzong's sixteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yong, Lin, was Xuanzong's sixteenth son.

sentences.zh: 母曰郭順儀，劍南節度尚書虛己之妹。

translations.literal: His mother was Lady Guo Shun, younger sister of Xuji, military commissioner of Jiannan and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Guo Shun, younger sister of Xuji, who served as military commissioner of Jiannan and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 璘數歲失母，肅宗收養，夜自抱眠之。

translations.literal: Lin lost his mother at several years of age. Suzong took him in to raise and at night would hold him in his arms to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Lin lost his mother while still a small child. Suzong took him in and would hold him in his arms at night to sleep.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏好學，貌陋，視物不正。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and fond of learning, but his appearance was homely and he did not see straight.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was clever and eager to learn, but his features were plain and his eyes did not align properly.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年三月，封為永王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, 725, he was created Prince of Yong.

sentences.zh: 十五年五月，遙領荊州大都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year, he held in title the post of Grand Protector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year, 727, he was given nominal appointment as Grand Protector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十年七月，加開府儀同三司，改名璘。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twentieth year, he was given the additional title of Grand Master with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank, and his name was changed to Lin.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twentieth year, 732, he was additionally appointed Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank, and his name was changed to Lin.

sentences.zh: 天寶十四載十一月，安祿山反范陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourteenth year of Tianbao, An Lushan rebelled at Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourteenth year of Tianbao, 755, An Lushan rebelled at Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 十五載六月，玄宗幸蜀，至漢中郡，下詔以璘為山南東路及嶺南黔中江南西路四道節度采訪等使、江陵郡大都督，余如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year, Xuanzong went to Shu. Reaching Hanzhong commandery, he issued an edict making Lin commissioner for investigation and military affairs over the four circuits of Shannan East, Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Jiangnan West, and Grand Protector of Jiangling commandery; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year, 756, Xuanzong fled to Shu. At Hanzhong he issued an edict appointing Lin commissioner for investigation and military affairs over the four circuits of Shannan East, Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Jiangnan West, and Grand Protector of Jiangling; his other titles were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 璘七月至襄陽，九月至江陵，召募士將數萬人，恣情補署，江淮租賦，山積於江陵，破用鉅億。

translations.literal: Lin reached Xiangyang in the seventh month and Jiangling in the ninth. He recruited officers and soldiers numbering tens of thousands, appointing posts at will. River and Huai tax revenues piled up at Jiangling like mountains, and he squandered hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Lin reached Xiangyang in the seventh month and Jiangling in the ninth. He recruited tens of thousands of officers and soldiers and filled posts at his pleasure. Tax revenues from the Yangzi and Huai regions piled up at Jiangling like mountains, and he squandered hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 以薛镠、李臺卿、蔡坰為謀主，因有異志。

translations.literal: He took Xue Liu, Li Taiqing, and Cai Jiong as chief strategists and thereby harbored divergent ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: He took Xue Liu, Li Taiqing, and Cai Jiong as his chief advisers and thus conceived rebellious designs.

sentences.zh: 肅宗聞之，詔令歸覲於蜀，璘不從命。

translations.literal: Suzong heard of it and issued an edict ordering him to return to court at Shu. Lin did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong learned of this, he ordered Lin to return to court at Shu. Lin refused.

sentences.zh: 十二月，擅領舟師東下，甲仗五千人趨廣陵，以季廣琛、渾惟明、高仙琦為將。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, he on his own authority led a fleet eastward. Five thousand men in armor and arms hastened to Guangling, with Ji Guangchen, Hun Weiming, and Gao Xianqi as generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he led a fleet eastward on his own authority. Five thousand armed men marched on Guangling under the generals Ji Guangchen, Hun Weiming, and Gao Xianqi.

sentences.zh: 璘生於宮中，不更人事，其子襄城王亻易又勇而有力，馭兵權，為左右眩惑，遂謀狂悖。

translations.literal: Lin had been born in the palace and had not experienced the affairs of the world. His son, Prince of Xiangcheng Yi, was again brave and strong, wielded military authority, was dazzled and misled by those around him, and thus plotted madness and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had been born in the palace and knew nothing of the world outside. His son, the Prince of Xiangcheng, Yi, was bold and strong, held military power, and was led astray by his advisers until they plotted open rebellion.

sentences.zh: 璘雖有窺江左之心，而未露其事。

translations.literal: Although Lin harbored a mind to covet the lands south of the Yangzi, he had not yet revealed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Although Lin harbored designs on the lands south of the Yangzi, he had not yet revealed his intent.

sentences.zh: 吳郡采訪使李希言乃平牒璘，大署其名，璘遂激怒，牒報曰：「寡人上皇天屬，皇帝友於，地尊侯王，禮絕僚品，簡書來往，應有常儀，今乃平牒抗威，落筆署字，漢儀隳紊，一至於斯！

translations.literal: Li Xiyan, commissioner for investigation of Wujun commandery, then sent Lin a dispatch on equal footing and signed his own name large upon it. Lin was enraged and replied by dispatch: "I, the orphan, am Heaven's kin to the Retired Emperor and a brother in affection to the Emperor. In rank I stand above feudal lords; in ritual I am set apart from the official grades. Written communications passing back and forth ought to observe fixed forms. Now you send a dispatch on equal footing to display authority, setting down your brush to sign your name—Han ritual is thrown into disorder to such a degree!
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiyan, commissioner for investigation of Wujun, sent Lin a dispatch on equal footing and signed his own name large upon it. Lin was furious and replied: "I am kin by Heaven to the Retired Emperor and a brother in affection to the reigning emperor. In rank I stand above feudal lords; in ritual I am set apart from the official grades. Written communications ought to observe proper forms. Yet you send a dispatch on equal footing to flaunt your authority, setting down your brush to sign your name—court ritual is thrown into disorder to such a degree!

sentences.zh: 」乃使渾惟明取希言，季廣琛趣廣陵攻采訪李成式。

translations.literal: " He then sent Hun Weiming to seize Xiyan and Ji Guangchen to hurry to Guangling to attack the commissioner for investigation Li Chengshi.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent Hun Weiming to seize Xiyan and Ji Guangchen to hurry to Guangling and attack the commissioner for investigation Li Chengshi.

sentences.zh: 璘進至當塗，希言在丹陽，令元景曜、閻敬之等以兵拒之，身走吳郡，李成式使將李承慶拒之。

translations.literal: Lin advanced to Dangtu. Xiyan was at Danyang and ordered Yuan Jingyao, Yan Jingzhi, and others to resist with troops. He himself fled to Wujun. Li Chengshi sent the general Li Chengqing to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Lin advanced to Dangtu. Xiyan was at Danyang and ordered Yuan Jingyao, Yan Jingzhi, and others to resist with troops while he himself fled to Wujun. Li Chengshi sent the general Li Chengqing to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 先是，肅宗以璘不受命，先使中官啖廷瑤、段喬福招討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Lin did not accept orders, Suzong had first sent the eunuchs Dan Tingyao and Duan Qiaofu to campaign against and suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Lin had refused orders, Suzong had sent the eunuchs Dan Tingyao and Duan Qiaofu to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 中官至廣陵，反式括得馬數百匹。

translations.literal: When the eunuchs reached Guangling, Chengshi on the contrary rounded up several hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuchs reached Guangling, Chengshi instead mustered several hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 時河北招討判官、司虞郎中李銑在廣陵，瑤等結銑為兄弟，求之將兵。

translations.literal: At the time Li Xian, recruitment commissioner for Hebei and Gentleman of the Palace for Ceremonial, was at Guangling. Tingyao and the others bonded with Xian as sworn brothers and asked him to lead troops.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Xian, recruitment commissioner for Hebei and Gentleman of the Palace for Ceremonial, was at Guangling. Tingyao and the others swore brotherhood with him and asked him to lead troops.

sentences.zh: 銑麾下有騎一百八十人，遂率所領屯於楊子，成式使判官評事裴茂以廣陵步卒三千同拒於瓜步洲伊婁埭。

translations.literal: Under Xian's command were one hundred eighty horsemen. He then led those under him to encamp at Yangzi. Chengshi sent his aide Pei Mao with three thousand Guangling foot soldiers to resist together at Yilou embankment on Guazhou isle.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had one hundred eighty horsemen under his command. He led them to encamp at Yangzi. Chengshi sent his aide Pei Mao with three thousand Guangling foot soldiers to join in resisting at Yilou embankment on Guazhou isle.

sentences.zh: 希言將元景曜及成式將李神慶並以其眾迎降於璘，璘又殺丹徒太守閻敬之以徇。

translations.literal: Xiyan's general Yuan Jingyao and Chengshi's general Li Shenqing all brought their forces to surrender to Lin. Lin also killed Yan Jingzhi, administrator of Dantu, as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyan's general Yuan Jingyao and Chengshi's general Li Shenqing both brought their forces to surrender to Lin. Lin also executed Yan Jingzhi, administrator of Dantu, as a warning to others.

sentences.zh: 江左大駭。

translations.literal: The lands south of the Yangzi were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The entire region south of the Yangzi was thrown into terror.

sentences.zh: 裴茂至瓜步洲，廣張旗幟，耀於江津。

translations.literal: Pei Mao reached Guazhou isle, spread banners wide, and displayed them shining at the river crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mao reached Guazhou isle, spread his banners wide, and displayed them glittering along the river crossing.

sentences.zh: 璘與亻易登陴望之竟日，始有懼色。

translations.literal: Lin and Yi ascended the wall and gazed at them all day before fear first showed on their faces.
translations.idiomatic: Lin and Yi climbed the ramparts and gazed at them all day before fear first showed on their faces.

sentences.zh: 季廣琛召諸將割臂而盟，以貳於璘。

translations.literal: Ji Guangchen summoned the generals to cut their arms and swear an oath, thereby turning against Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Guangchen summoned the generals to cut their arms and swear an oath, thereby turning against Lin.

sentences.zh: 是日，渾惟明走於江寧，馮季康、康謙投於廣陵之白沙。

translations.literal: That day, Hun Weiming fled to Jiangning. Feng Jikang and Kang Qian surrendered at Baisha in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: That day Hun Weiming fled to Jiangning, while Feng Jikang and Kang Qian surrendered at Baisha in Guangling.

sentences.zh: 廣琛以步卒六千趨廣陵，璘使騎追之，廣琛曰：「我感王恩，是以不能決戰，逃而歸國。

translations.literal: Guangchen led six thousand foot soldiers toward Guangling. Lin sent cavalry in pursuit. Guangchen said: "I am moved by the prince's grace and therefore cannot join battle decisively. I flee to return to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchen led six thousand foot soldiers toward Guangling. Lin sent cavalry in pursuit. Guangchen said, "I am moved by the prince's grace and therefore cannot bring myself to fight. I flee only to return to the lawful court.

sentences.zh: 若逼我，我則不擇地而回戰矣。

translations.literal: If you press me, I will not choose the ground before turning to fight.
translations.idiomatic: If you press me, I will turn and fight wherever I stand.

sentences.zh: 」使者返報。

translations.literal: " The messenger returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: " The messenger returned with his report.

sentences.zh: 其夕，銑等多燃火，人執兩炬以疑之，隔江望者，兼水中之影，一皆為二矣。

translations.literal: That evening, Xian and the others lit many fires. Each man held two torches to create doubt. Those gazing across the river, together with the reflections in the water, all saw each as two.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Xian and the others lit many fires, and each man held two torches to create confusion. Those watching from across the river, together with the reflections in the water, saw every flame doubled.

sentences.zh: 璘軍又以火應之。

translations.literal: Lin's army also answered with fire.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's army answered with fires of their own.

sentences.zh: 璘懼，以官軍悉濟矣，遂以兒女及麾下宵遁。

translations.literal: Lin was afraid, thinking the government army had all crossed over. He then fled by night with his children and followers.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was afraid, believing the government army had all crossed the river. He fled by night with his children and followers.

sentences.zh: 遲明，不見濟者，遂入城具舟楫，使襄城王驅其眾以奔晉陵。

translations.literal: At dawn, seeing no one had crossed, he entered the city to prepare boats and oars and ordered the Prince of Xiangcheng to drive his troops to flee toward Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, seeing that no one had crossed, he entered the city to prepare boats and ordered the Prince of Xiangcheng to drive his troops toward Jinling.

sentences.zh: 宵諜曰：「王走矣。

translations.literal: A night spy said: "The prince has fled.
translations.idiomatic: A night scout reported, "The prince has fled.

sentences.zh: 」於是江北之軍齊進，募敢死士趙侃、庫狄岫、趙連城等共二十人，先鋒遊弈於新豐，皆因醉而寐。

translations.literal: " Then the army north of the river advanced together. They recruited dare-to-die men Zhao Kan, Kudixiu, Zhao Liancheng, and twenty others in all. The vanguard ranged at Xinfeng, and all because of drink fell asleep.
translations.idiomatic: " The army north of the river then advanced together. They recruited twenty dare-to-die men including Zhao Kan, Kudixiu, and Zhao Liancheng. The vanguard ranged at Xinfeng, and all, drunk, fell asleep.

sentences.zh: 璘聞官軍之至，乃使襄城王、高仙琦逆擊之。

translations.literal: Lin heard the government army had arrived and sent the Prince of Xiangcheng and Gao Xianqi to strike them in counterattack.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin heard the government army had arrived, he sent the Prince of Xiangcheng and Gao Xianqi to meet them in counterattack.

sentences.zh: 驛騎奔告，侃等介馬而出，襄城王已隨而至，銑等奔救，張左右翼擊之，射中襄城王首，亻易軍遂敗。

translations.literal: Courier riders came galloping to report. Kan and the others mounted in armor and sallied forth. The Prince of Xiangcheng had already followed close behind. Xian and the others ran to the rescue, deployed left and right wings to strike, and shot the Prince of Xiangcheng in the head. Yi's army was then defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Courier riders came galloping with the news. Kan and the others mounted in armor and sallied forth. The Prince of Xiangcheng was already close behind. Xian and the others rushed to the rescue, deployed wings on both flanks, and shot the Prince of Xiangcheng in the head. Yi's army was routed.

sentences.zh: 高仙琦等四騎與璘南奔，至鄱陽郡，司馬陶備閉城拒之。

translations.literal: Gao Xianqi and four horsemen fled south with Lin. Reaching Poyang commandery, the aide Tao Bei closed the city and refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xianqi and four horsemen fled south with Lin. At Poyang commandery the aide Tao Bei closed the city against them.

sentences.zh: 璘怒，命焚其城。

translations.literal: Lin was angry and ordered the city burned.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was furious and ordered the city burned.

sentences.zh: 至余幹，及大庾嶺，將南投嶺外，為江西采訪使皇甫侁下防禦兵所擒，因中矢而薨。

translations.literal: Reaching Yugan and the Dayu Range, about to flee south beyond the ranges, he was seized by defensive troops sent by Huangfu Shen, commissioner for investigation of Jiangxi. He died from an arrow wound.
translations.idiomatic: At Yugan and the Dayu Range, as he was about to flee south beyond the mountains, he was seized by defensive troops sent by Huangfu Shen, commissioner for investigation of Jiangxi, and died of an arrow wound.

sentences.zh: 子亻易等為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: His son Yi and others were killed by mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi and others were killed by mutinous soldiers.

sentences.zh: 肅宗以璘愛弟，隱而不言。

translations.literal: Suzong, because Lin was a beloved younger brother, concealed the matter and did not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Because Lin had been a beloved younger brother, Suzong concealed the matter and did not speak of it.

sentences.zh: 壽王瑁，玄宗第十八子也，初名清。

translations.literal: Prince of Shou Mao was Emperor Xuanzong's eighteenth son; his original name was Qing.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shou, Mao, was Xuanzong's eighteenth son. His birth name was Qing.

sentences.zh: 初，瑁母武惠妃，開元元年見幸，寵傾後宮，頻產夏悼王、懷哀王、上仙公主，皆端麗，繈褓不育。

translations.literal: Earlier, Mao's mother Consort Wu Huifei, favored in the first year of Kaiyuan, had favor that tilted the entire inner palace. She repeatedly bore the Xiaosi Prince, the Huai'ai Prince, and Princess Shangxian—all comely and fair—yet none survived swaddling clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Mao's mother, Consort Wu Huifei, had won favor in the first year of Kaiyuan and come to dominate the inner palace. She bore the Xiaosi Prince, the Huai'ai Prince, and Princess Shangxian in succession—all fair and comely—yet none survived infancy.

sentences.zh: 及瑁之初生，讓帝妃元氏請瑁在於邸中收養，妃自乳之，名為己子。

translations.literal: When Mao was first born, the Retired Emperor's consort, the Lady Yuan, asked to take Mao into her residence to raise him. The consort herself nursed him and named him as her own son.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao was born, the Retired Emperor's consort, Lady Yuan of the Yuan clan, asked to raise him in her own residence. She nursed him herself and treated him as her own son.

sentences.zh: 十余年在寧邸，故封建之事晚於諸王。

translations.literal: For more than ten years he was at the Ning residence, and therefore his enfeoffment came later than the other princes.
translations.idiomatic: He spent more than ten years in the Ning residence, and therefore his enfeoffment came later than the other princes.

sentences.zh: 宮中常呼為十八郎。

translations.literal: Within the palace he was commonly called the Eighteenth Lad.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace he was commonly called the Eighteenth Lad.

sentences.zh: 十三年三月，封為壽王，始入宮中。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shou and first entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirteenth year, 725, he was created Prince of Shou and first entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遙領益州大都督、劍南節度大使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he held in title the posts of Grand Protector of Yizhou and military commissioner of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, 727, he was given nominal appointment as Grand Protector of Yizhou and military commissioner of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加開府儀同三司，改名瑁。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was given the additional title of Grand Master with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank, and his name was changed to Mao.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, 735, he was additionally appointed Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank, and his name was changed to Mao.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，惠妃薨，葬以後禮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Huifei died and was buried with the rites of an empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, 737, Huifei died and was buried with the rites due an empress.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，讓帝薨，瑁請制服，以報乳養之恩，玄宗從之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the Retired Emperor died. Mao requested mourning garments to repay the grace of nursing and rearing, and Xuanzong consented.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, 741, the Retired Emperor died. Mao asked to wear mourning garments in return for the grace of having been nursed and reared, and Xuanzong consented.

sentences.zh: 瑁，天寶中有子封為王者二人：懷為濟陽郡王，偡為廣陽郡王、鴻臚卿同正員。

translations.literal: Mao, in the Tianbao period, had two sons enfeoffed as princes: Huai as Prince of Jiyang commandery, and Xu as Prince of Guangyang commandery and Acting Regular Minister of the Court for Diplomatic Reception.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era, two of Mao's sons were created princes: Huai as Prince of Jiyang, and Xu as Prince of Guangyang with the acting rank of Minister of the Court for Diplomatic Reception.

sentences.zh: 唐法，親王食封八百戶，有至一千戶；

translations.literal: Under Tang law, imperial princes received enfeoffment income of eight hundred households, with some reaching one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang law, imperial princes received enfeoffment income of eight hundred households, though some received as many as one thousand.

sentences.zh: 公主三百戶，長公主加三百戶，有至六百戶。

translations.literal: Princesses received three hundred households; senior princesses received an additional three hundred, with some reaching six hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses received three hundred households; senior princesses received an additional three hundred, for a total of up to six hundred.

sentences.zh: 高宗朝以沛、英、豫王、太平公主武後所生，食逾於制。

translations.literal: In the Gaozong reign, because the Princes of Pei, Ying, and Yu and Princess Taiping were born of Empress Wu, their incomes exceeded the regulation.
translations.idiomatic: During Gaozong's reign, because the Princes of Pei, Ying, and Yu and Princess Taiping were born of Empress Wu, their incomes exceeded the statutory limit.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，太平至一千二百戶。

translations.literal: In the Chuigong period, Taiping reached one thousand two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuigong era, Taiping's income reached one thousand two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 聖歷初，皇嗣封為相王，食封與太平同三千戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenglü era, the heir apparent was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiang, with enfeoffment income equal to Taiping's at three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenglü era, the heir apparent was created Prince of Xiang with enfeoffment income equal to Taiping's at three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 長安中，壽春王兄弟五人，並賜實封三百戶。

translations.literal: In the Chang'an period, the five brothers of the Prince of Shouchun were all granted actual enfeoffment of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era, the five brothers of the Prince of Shouchun were each granted actual enfeoffment of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，相府與太平同至五千戶，衛王三千戶，溫王二千戶，成王七百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, the Xiang residence and Taiping alike reached five thousand households; the Prince of Wei three thousand; the Prince of Wen two thousand; the Prince of Cheng seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, the Xiang residence and Taiping alike reached five thousand households; the Prince of Wei three thousand; the Prince of Wen two thousand; and the Prince of Cheng seven hundred.

sentences.zh: 壽春王加四百戶，通前七百戶；

translations.literal: The Prince of Shouchun received an additional four hundred households, totaling seven hundred with what he had before.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shouchun received an additional four hundred households, bringing his total to seven hundred.

sentences.zh: 嗣雍、衡陽、臨淄、巴陵、中山各加二百戶，通前五百戶。

translations.literal: Siyong, Hengyang, Linzi, Baling, and Zhongshan each received an additional two hundred households, totaling five hundred with what they had before.
translations.idiomatic: Siyong, Hengyang, Linzi, Baling, and Zhongshan each received an additional two hundred households, bringing their totals to five hundred each.

sentences.zh: 安樂初封二千戶，長寧一千五百戶，宣城、宜城、宣安各一千戶，相王女為縣主者各三百戶。

translations.literal: Anle at first enfeoffment received two thousand households; Changning one thousand five hundred; Xuancheng, Yicheng, and Xuan'an each one thousand; daughters of the Prince of Xiang enfeoffed as county mistresses each three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Anle at first enfeoffment received two thousand households; Changning one thousand five hundred; Xuancheng, Yicheng, and Xuan'an each one thousand; and daughters of the Prince of Xiang created county mistresses each three hundred.

sentences.zh: 衛王尋升儲位，相府增至七千戶，太平至五千戶，安樂三千戶，長寧二千五百戶，宣城已下各二千戶。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wei soon ascended the heir apparent's position. The Xiang residence was increased to seven thousand households; Taiping to five thousand; Anle to three thousand; Changning to two thousand five hundred; Xuancheng and below each to two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wei soon became heir apparent, the Xiang residence was increased to seven thousand households; Taiping to five thousand; Anle to three thousand; Changning to two thousand five hundred; and Xuancheng and below each to two thousand.

sentences.zh: 相府、太平、長寧、安樂皆以七千為限，雖水旱亦不破損免，以正租庸充數。

translations.literal: The Xiang residence, Taiping, Changning, and Anle all took seven thousand as the limit. Even in flood or drought they were not reduced or exempted; regular tax and corvée labor supplied the count.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiang residence, Taiping, Changning, and Anle all had seven thousand as their ceiling. Even in years of flood or drought their incomes were not reduced or exempted; regular tax and corvée revenues made up the allotted amount.

sentences.zh: 唐隆元年，遺制以嗣雍王守禮、壽春王成器封為親王，各賜實封一千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tanglong, the testamentary decree enfeoffed Siyong Prince Shouli and Shouchun Prince Chengqi as imperial princes, each granted actual enfeoffment of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tanglong, 710, the testamentary decree created Siyong Prince Shouli and Shouchun Prince Chengqi as imperial princes, each granted actual enfeoffment of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 開元之後，朝恩睦親，以寧府最長，封至五千五百戶；

translations.literal: After Kaiyuan, the court favored kinship and amity. Because the Ning residence was eldest, enfeoffment reached five thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After Kaiyuan, the court favored kinship and amity. Because the Ning residence was the senior line, its enfeoffment reached five thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 岐、薛愛弟著勛，五千戶；

translations.literal: Qi and Xue, beloved younger brothers with recorded merit, five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and Xue, beloved younger brothers with recorded merit, received five thousand households each.

sentences.zh: 申府以外家微，至四千戶；

translations.literal: The Shen residence, because the maternal kin were slight, reached four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The Shen residence, because the maternal kin were of modest standing, received up to four thousand households.

sentences.zh: 邠府以外枝，至一千八百戶。

translations.literal: The Bin residence, as a collateral branch, reached one thousand eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The Bin residence, as a collateral branch, received up to one thousand eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 皇妹為公主者，食封一千戶，中宗女亦同。

translations.literal: Imperial younger sisters made princesses received enfeoffment income of one thousand households; daughters of Zhongzong were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial younger sisters created princesses received enfeoffment income of one thousand households; daughters of Emperor Zhongzong were treated the same.

sentences.zh: 其後，皇子封王者賜封二千戶，皇女為公主者賜封五百戶。

translations.literal: Thereafter, imperial sons enfeoffed as princes were granted enfeoffment of two thousand households; imperial daughters made princesses were granted five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, imperial sons created princes were granted enfeoffment of two thousand households; imperial daughters created princesses were granted five hundred.

sentences.zh: 咸宜賜湯沐，以母惠妃封至一千戶，諸皇女為公主者，例加至一千戶。

translations.literal: Xianyi was granted bath and maintenance revenues. Because her mother was Huifei, enfeoffment reached one thousand households. All imperial daughters made princesses were by precedent increased to one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Xianyi was granted bath and maintenance revenues. Because her mother was Huifei, her enfeoffment reached one thousand households. All imperial daughters created princesses were by precedent increased to one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 其封自開元已來，皆約以三千為限。

translations.literal: Their enfeoffments from Kaiyuan onward were all roughly limited to three thousand as the ceiling.
translations.idiomatic: From Kaiyuan onward, enfeoffments were generally capped at three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 延王玢，玄宗第二十子也，初名洄。

translations.literal: Prince of Yan Bin was Emperor Xuanzong's twentieth son; his original name was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan, Bin, was Xuanzong's twentieth son. His birth name was Hui.

sentences.zh: 玢母即尚書右丞柳範孫也，最為名家，玄宗深重之。

translations.literal: Bin's mother was the granddaughter of Vice Minister of the Right Liu Fan and came from the most eminent of families. Xuanzong held her in deep regard.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's mother was the granddaughter of Vice Minister of the Right Liu Fan and came from one of the most eminent families of the age. Xuanzong held her in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 玢亦仁愛，有學問。

translations.literal: Bin was also benevolent and had learning.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was likewise benevolent and learned.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年，封為延王。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, 725, he was created Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遙領安西大都護、磧西節度大使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he held in title the posts of Grand Protector of Anxi and military commissioner of Qixi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, 727, he was given nominal appointment as Grand Protector of Anxi and military commissioner of Qixi.

sentences.zh: 二十三年七月，加開府儀同三司，余如故，改名玢。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year, he was given the additional title of Grand Master with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank; the rest remained as before, and his name was changed to Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year, 735, he was additionally appointed Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank; his other titles were unchanged, and his name was changed to Bin.

sentences.zh: 天寶十五載，玄宗幸蜀，玢男女三十六人，不忍棄於道路，數日不及行在所，玄宗怒之；

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianbao, Xuanzong went to Shu. Bin's sons and daughters, thirty-six in all, he could not bear to abandon on the road. For several days he did not reach the imperial encampment. Xuanzong was angry with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Tianbao, 756, when Xuanzong fled to Shu, Bin could not bear to leave his thirty-six sons and daughters on the road. For several days he failed to reach the imperial encampment, and Xuanzong was furious.

sentences.zh: 賴漢中王瑀抗疏救之，聽歸於靈武。

translations.literal: Thanks to Prince of Hanzhong Yu's bold memorial in his defense, he was permitted to return to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the Prince of Hanzhong, Yu, submitted a bold memorial in his defense was he permitted to return to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 興元元年薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Xingyuan era, 784.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，封子倬彭城郡王、秘書監同正員，亻延平陽郡王、殿中監同正員。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao, his sons Zhuo was enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng commandery and Acting Regular Director of the Secretariat, and Yan as Prince of Pingyang commandery and Acting Regular Director of the Palace Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era, his son Zhuo was created Prince of Pengcheng with the acting rank of Director of the Secretariat, and Yan as Prince of Pingyang with the acting rank of Director of the Palace Bureau.

sentences.zh: 盛王琦，玄宗第二十一子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Sheng Qi was Emperor Xuanzong's twenty-first son.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Sheng, Qi, was Xuanzong's twenty-first son.

sentences.zh: 壽王母弟，初名沐。

translations.literal: He was the Prince of Shou's younger brother by the same mother; his original name was Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was the younger brother of the Prince of Shou by the same mother. His birth name was Mu.

sentences.zh: 十三年三月，封為盛王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, 725, he was created Prince of Sheng.

sentences.zh: 十五年，領揚州大都督。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he held the post of Grand Protector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, 727, he was appointed Grand Protector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十年，加開府儀同三司，余如故，改名琦。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he was given the additional title of Grand Master with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank; the rest remained as before, and his name was changed to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, 732, he was additionally appointed Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank; his other titles were unchanged, and his name was changed to Qi.

sentences.zh: 天寶十五年六月，玄宗幸蜀，在路除琦為廣陵大都督，仍領江南東路及淮南河南等路節度支度采訪等使，以前江陵大都督府長史劉匯為之副，以廣陵長史李成式為副大使、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year of Tianbao, Xuanzong went to Shu. On the road Qi was appointed Grand Protector of Guangling and still held the posts of commissioner for investigation, military affairs, and fiscal administration over Jiangnan East, Huainan, Henan, and other circuits. The former senior administrator of the Jiangling Grand Protectorate, Liu Hui, was made his deputy, and Guangling senior administrator Li Chengshi was made deputy commissioner and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year of Tianbao, 756, as Xuanzong fled to Shu, Qi was appointed Grand Protector of Guangling on the road and given command as commissioner for investigation, military affairs, and fiscal administration over Jiangnan East, Huainan, Henan, and other circuits. The former senior administrator of the Jiangling protectorate, Liu Hui, was made his deputy, and Guangling senior administrator Li Chengshi was made deputy commissioner with concurrent appointment as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 琦竟不行。

translations.literal: Qi in the end did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Qi never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年四月薨，贈太傅。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Guangde he died and was posthumously given the title Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of the second year of Guangde, 764, and was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 天寶末有子封王者二人：償真定郡王、太常卿同正員，佩封武都郡王、殿中監同正員。
