translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he had two sons enfeoffed as princes: Chang as Prince of Zhending commandery and Acting Regular Minister of Ceremonial; Pei as Prince of Wudu commandery and Acting Regular Director of the Palace Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era, two of his sons were created princes: Chang as Prince of Zhending with the acting rank of Minister of Ceremonial, and Pei as Prince of Wudu with the acting rank of Director of the Palace Bureau.

sentences.zh: 濟王環，玄宗第二十二子也，初名溢。

translations.literal: Prince of Ji Huan was Emperor Xuanzong's twenty-second son; his original name was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ji, Huan, was Xuanzong's twenty-second son. His birth name was Yi.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年三月，封濟王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, 725, he was created Prince of Ji.

sentences.zh: 二十三年七月，授開府儀同三司，其月改名環。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year, he was given the title Grand Master with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank. That month his name was changed to Huan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year, 735, he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank, and that same month his name was changed to Huan.

sentences.zh: 天寶末有子封為王者二人，傃為永嘉郡王、衛尉卿同正員，俛為平樂郡王、光祿卿同正員。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he had two sons enfeoffed as princes: Su as Prince of Yongjia commandery and Acting Regular Minister of the Guard; Mian as Prince of Pingle commandery and Acting Regular Commissioner of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era, two of his sons were created princes: Su as Prince of Yongjia with the acting rank of Minister of the Guard, and Mian as Prince of Pingle with the acting rank of Commissioner of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 信王瑝，玄宗第二十三子也，初名沔。

translations.literal: Prince of Xin Huang was Emperor Xuanzong's twenty-third son; his original name was Mian.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xin, Huang, was Xuanzong's twenty-third son. His birth name was Mian.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年三月，封為信王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, 725, he was created Prince of Xin.

sentences.zh: 二十三年七月，授開府儀同三司，仍改名瑝。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year, he was given the title Grand Master with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank, and his name was still changed to Huang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year, 735, he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank, and his name was changed to Huang.

sentences.zh: 天寶末有子封為王者二人：亻冬為新安郡王、太常卿同正員，倜為晉陵郡王、光祿卿同正員。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he had two sons enfeoffed as princes: Dong as Prince of Xin'an commandery and Acting Regular Minister of Ceremonial; Ti as Prince of Jinling commandery and Acting Regular Commissioner of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era, two of his sons were created princes: Dong as Prince of Xin'an with the acting rank of Minister of Ceremonial, and Ti as Prince of Jinling with the acting rank of Commissioner of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 義王玭，玄宗第二十四子也，初名漼。

translations.literal: Prince of Yi Mi was Emperor Xuanzong's twenty-fourth son; his original name was Cui.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yi, Mi, was Xuanzong's twenty-fourth son. His birth name was Cui.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年三月，封為義王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, 725, he was created Prince of Yi.

sentences.zh: 二十三年七月，授開府儀同三司，仍改名玭。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year, he was given the title Grand Master with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank, and his name was still changed to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year, 735, he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank, and his name was changed to Mi.

sentences.zh: 天寶末有子封為王者二人：儀為舞陽郡王、太仆卿同正員，僇為高密郡王、宗正卿同正員。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he had two sons enfeoffed as princes: Yi as Prince of Wuyang commandery and Acting Regular Minister of the Stud; Lu as Prince of Gaomi commandery and Acting Regular Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era, two of his sons were created princes: Yi as Prince of Wuyang with the acting rank of Minister of the Stud, and Lu as Prince of Gaomi with the acting rank of Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 陳王珪，玄宗第二十五子也，初名渙。

translations.literal: Prince of Chen Gui was Emperor Xuanzong's twenty-fifth son; his original name was Huan.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Chen, Gui, was Xuanzong's twenty-fifth son. His birth name was Huan.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年七月，封為陳王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, 735, he was created Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 二十四年三月改名珪。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-fourth year, his name was changed to Gui.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-fourth year, 736, his name was changed to Gui.

sentences.zh: 天寶末男女二十一人，封為王者二人：佗為臨淮郡王、太常卿同正員，佼為安陽王、殿中監同正員。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he had twenty-one sons and daughters. Two were enfeoffed as princes: Tuo as Prince of Linhuai commandery and Acting Regular Minister of Ceremonial; Jiao as Prince of Anyang and Acting Regular Director of the Palace Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era he had twenty-one sons and daughters. Two sons were created princes: Tuo as Prince of Linhuai with the acting rank of Minister of Ceremonial, and Jiao as Prince of Anyang with the acting rank of Director of the Palace Bureau.

sentences.zh: 豐王珙，玄宗第二十六子也，初名澄。

translations.literal: Prince of Feng Gong was Emperor Xuanzong's twenty-sixth son; his original name was Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Feng, Gong, was Xuanzong's twenty-sixth son. His birth name was Cheng.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年七月，封為豐王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Feng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, 735, he was created Prince of Feng.

sentences.zh: 二十四年二月改名珙。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-fourth year, his name was changed to Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-fourth year, 736, his name was changed to Gong.

sentences.zh: 天寶十五年六月，玄宗幸蜀，至扶風郡，授珙武威郡都督，仍領河西隴右安西北庭等路節度支度采訪使；

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year of Tianbao, Xuanzong went to Shu. Reaching Fufeng commandery, he appointed Gong governor of Wuwei commandery and still commissioner for investigation, military affairs, and fiscal administration over Hexi, Longyou, Anbei, Beiting, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year of Tianbao, 756, as Xuanzong fled to Shu, at Fufeng commandery he appointed Gong governor of Wuwei and commissioner for investigation, military affairs, and fiscal administration over Hexi, Longyou, Anbei, Beiting, and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 以隴右太守鄧景山為之副，兼武威長史、御史中丞，充都副大使。

translations.literal: Deng Jingshan, administrator of Longyou, was made his deputy, with concurrent posts as senior administrator of Wuwei and Censor-in-Chief, serving as overall deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jingshan, administrator of Longyou, was made his deputy with concurrent appointment as senior administrator of Wuwei and Censor-in-Chief, serving as overall deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 珙竟不行。

translations.literal: Gong in the end did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Gong never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年十月，吐蕃淩逼上都，上將幸陜州，自苑中而出，騎從半渡浐水。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Guangde, the Tibetans pressed upon the upper capital. The emperor was about to go to Shaanzhou and came out from within the park. The mounted escort had half crossed the Chan River.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Guangde, 763, as the Tibetans pressed upon the capital, the emperor prepared to flee to Shaanzhou and came out from within the imperial park. His mounted escort had half crossed the Chan River.

sentences.zh: 將軍王懷忠遂閉苑門，橫截五百余騎，擁十宅諸王西投吐蕃。

translations.literal: General Wang Huaizhong then closed the park gates, cut across more than five hundred horsemen, and escorted the princes of the Ten Residences west to surrender to the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Huaizhong then closed the park gates, intercepted more than five hundred horsemen, and drove the princes of the Ten Residences west to surrender to the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 至城西，適遇元帥郭子儀，懷忠謂子儀曰：「主上東遷，社稷無主，萬國颙颙，何所瞻仰！

translations.literal: Reaching the west of the city, they happened upon the commander Guo Ziyi. Huaizhong said to Ziyi: "The sovereign has moved east. The altars of state have no master. The ten thousand states look up longingly—upon whom can they gaze?
translations.idiomatic: At the west of the city they happened upon the commander Guo Ziyi. Huaizhong said to him, "The sovereign has moved east. The altars of state stand without a master. The realm looks up in longing—upon whom can they gaze?

sentences.zh: 今仆奉諸王等西奔，以副天下之望。

translations.literal: Now your servant leads the princes and others west in flight to answer the hopes of all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I now lead these princes west to answer the hopes of the realm.

sentences.zh: 令公身為元帥，廢置在手，何不行冊立之事乎？

translations.literal: Your Lordship stands as commander; deposition and installation are in your hands—why not perform the rite of enthronement?
translations.idiomatic: Your Lordship stands as commander, with deposition and installation in your hands—why not perform the rite of enthronement?

sentences.zh: 」子儀未及對，珙遂越次而言曰：「令公作何語，何不言也？

translations.literal: " Before Ziyi could reply, Gong stepped forward out of turn and said: "What words does Your Lordship speak? Why do you not speak?
translations.idiomatic: " Before Ziyi could reply, Gong stepped forward out of turn and said, "What is Your Lordship saying? Why do you not speak?

sentences.zh: 」行軍司馬王延昌責之曰：「主上雖蒙塵於外，聖德欽明，王身為籓翰，何乃發狂悖之詞也？

translations.literal: " Campaign aide Wang Yanchang reproached him: "Although the sovereign suffers dust abroad, his sagely virtue is revered and bright. Your Highness stands as a screen for the realm—how can you utter words of madness and rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: " Campaign aide Wang Yanchang reproached him: "Although the sovereign suffers hardship abroad, his sagely virtue remains revered and bright. Your Highness stands as a screen for the realm—how can you utter words of madness and rebellion?

sentences.zh: 延昌當奏聞於上。

translations.literal: Yanchang will memorialize and report this to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: I shall memorialize and report this to the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 」子儀又數讓之，命軍士領之盡赴行在。

translations.literal: " Ziyi again reproached him several times and ordered soldiers to lead them all to the imperial encampment.
translations.idiomatic: " Ziyi reproached him again and again and ordered soldiers to escort them all to the imperial encampment.

sentences.zh: 潼關謁見，上不之責，珙歸幕次，詞又不順。

translations.literal: At Tong Pass they had audience. The emperor did not blame him. Gong returned to his tent, and his words were again improper.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass they had audience with the emperor, who did not blame him. Gong returned to his quarters, but his words were again improper.

sentences.zh: 群臣恐遂為亂，請除之，遂賜死。

translations.literal: The ministers feared he would then make rebellion and requested his removal. He was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers feared he would then stir rebellion and requested his removal. He was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 天寶中有子二人為王：佻齊安郡王、宗正卿同正員，伷宜春郡王、鴻臚卿同正員。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao period he had two sons made princes: Tiao as Prince of Qi'an commandery and Acting Regular Director of the Imperial Clan; Zhou as Prince of Yichun commandery and Acting Regular Minister of the Court for Diplomatic Reception.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era he had two sons created princes: Tiao as Prince of Qi'an with the acting rank of Director of the Imperial Clan, and Zhou as Prince of Yichun with the acting rank of Minister of the Court for Diplomatic Reception.

sentences.zh: 恆王瑱，玄宗第二十七子也，初名潓。

translations.literal: Prince of Heng Zhen was Emperor Xuanzong's twenty-seventh son; his original name was Guan.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Heng, Zhen, was Xuanzong's twenty-seventh son. His birth name was Guan.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年七月，封為恆王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Heng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, 735, he was created Prince of Heng.

sentences.zh: 性好道，常服道士衣。

translations.literal: His nature favored the Way; he constantly wore Daoist robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to the Way and habitually wore Daoist robes.

sentences.zh: 授右衛大將軍，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Guard and given the additional title of Grand Master with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Guard and additionally given the rank of Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Girdle and Privy Seal of the First Rank.

sentences.zh: 二十四年二月改名瑱。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-fourth year, his name was changed to Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-fourth year, 736, his name was changed to Zhen.

sentences.zh: 天寶十五載，從幸巴蜀，不復衣道士衣矣。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianbao, he followed the imperial progress to Ba-Shu and no longer wore Daoist robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Tianbao, 756, he followed the flight to Ba-Shu and no longer wore Daoist robes.

sentences.zh: 涼王璿，玄宗第二十九子也，初名漎。

translations.literal: Prince of Liang Xuan was Emperor Xuanzong's twenty-ninth son; his original name was Long.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang, Xuan, was Xuanzong's twenty-ninth son. His birth name was Long.

sentences.zh: 母武賢儀，則天時高平王重規女也，開元中入宮中，號為「小武妃」。

translations.literal: His mother was Lady Wu Xian, daughter of Prince of Gaoping Chonggui in the time of Wu Zetian. In the Kaiyuan period she entered the palace and was called "Little Consort Wu."
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Wu Xian, daughter of Prince Chonggui of Gaoping in the time of Empress Wu. She entered the palace during Kaiyuan and was called "Little Consort Wu."

sentences.zh: 二十三年七月，封為涼王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year, 735, he was created Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 二十四年二月，改名璿。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-fourth year, his name was changed to Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-fourth year, 736, his name was changed to Xuan.

sentences.zh: 初，貞觀中，高宗為晉王，以文德皇后最少子，後崩後累年，太宗憐之，不令出閣，至立為太子。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Zhenguan period, when Gaozong was Prince of Jin, because Empress Wende was the youngest son, and after the empress died he passed many years, Taizong pitied him and did not let him leave the palace quarters until he was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Zhenguan era, when Gaozong was Prince of Jin, he was the youngest son of Empress Wende. After the empress died he remained in mourning for many years, and Taizong pitied him and would not let him leave the inner quarters until he was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 高宗朝，睿宗為豫王，雖成長，亦以則天最小子，不令出閣。

translations.literal: In the Gaozong reign, when Ruizong was Prince of Yu, although he had grown up, because he was Wu Zetian's youngest son, he was not let leave the palace quarters.
translations.idiomatic: During Gaozong's reign, when Ruizong was Prince of Yu, although he had come of age, as Wu Zetian's youngest son he was not permitted to leave the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 及至聖歷初，封為相王，始出閣。

translations.literal: Only at the beginning of the Shenglü era, when he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiang, did he first leave the palace quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the beginning of the Shenglü era, when he was created Prince of Xiang, did he first leave the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，以譙王重福失愛，出遷外籓，衛王重俊為太子，入與成王千里等起兵，將誅韋後，故溫王重茂雖年十六七，竟亦居中。

translations.literal: In Zhongzong's time, because Prince of Qiao Chongfu lost favor he was sent out to an outer fief. Prince of Wei Chongjun was crown prince and entered the palace. Together with Prince of Cheng Qianli and others he raised troops intending to execute Empress Wei. Therefore Prince of Wen Chongmao, though only sixteen or seventeen, in the end also remained within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhongzong's reign, because the Prince of Qiao, Chongfu, had lost favor he was sent to an outer fief. The Prince of Wei, Chongjun, as crown prince remained within the palace. When he joined the Prince of Cheng, Qianli, and others in raising troops to execute Empress Wei, the Prince of Wen, Chongmao, though only sixteen or seventeen, likewise remained within.

sentences.zh: 先天之後，皇子幼則居內，東封年，以漸成長，乃於安國寺東附苑城同為大宅，分院居，為十王宅。

translations.literal: After Xiantian, young imperial sons dwelt within. In the year of the eastern feng sacrifice, as they gradually grew up, east of Anguo Temple they attached to the park city wall and together made a great residence, dwelling in separate courtyards—this was the Ten Princes' Residence.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xiantian era, young imperial sons lived within the palace. In the year of the eastern feng sacrifice, as they gradually grew up, a great compound was built east of Anguo Temple against the park wall, with separate courtyards for each prince—the Ten Princes' Residence.

sentences.zh: 令中官押之，於夾城中起居，每日家令進膳。

translations.literal: Eunuchs were ordered to supervise them. They dwelled within the walled lane, and daily the household steward brought meals.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs were assigned to supervise them. They lived within the walled lane, and each day the household steward brought their meals.

sentences.zh: 又引詞學工書之人入教，謂之侍讀。

translations.literal: Men skilled in literary composition and calligraphy were also brought in to teach them; they were called lecturing attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars skilled in literary composition and calligraphy were brought in to instruct them; they were called lecturing attendants.

sentences.zh: 十王，謂慶、忠、棣、鄂、榮、光、儀、潁、永、延、濟，蓋舉全數。

translations.literal: The ten princes were called Qing, Zhong, Di, E, Rong, Guang, Yi, Ying, Yong, Yan, and Ji—roughly the full round number.
translations.idiomatic: The ten princes were Qing, Zhong, Di, E, Rong, Guang, Yi, Ying, Yong, Yan, and Ji—a round figure for the full complement.

sentences.zh: 其後，盛、儀、壽、陳、豐、恆、涼六王又就封，入內宅。

translations.literal: Thereafter the six princes Sheng, Yi, Shou, Chen, Feng, Heng, and Liang were in turn enfeoffed and entered the inner residence.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the six princes Sheng, Yi, Shou, Chen, Feng, Heng, and Liang were in turn enfeoffed and moved into the inner residence.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，鄂、光得罪，忠繼大統，天寶中，慶、棣又歿，唯榮、儀等十四王居院，而府幕列於外坊，時通名起居而已。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, E and Guang offended. Zhong succeeded to the great succession. In the Tianbao period, Qing and Di also died. Only Rong, Yi, and fourteen other princes dwelt in the residence, while their staff were arrayed in the outer wards. At the time they merely sent their names for attendance reports.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, 737, the Princes of E and Guang fell from favor. Zhong succeeded to the throne. During Tianbao, the Princes of Qing and Di also died. Only Rong, Yi, and fourteen other princes remained in the residence, while their staffs were posted in the outer wards and merely sent their names for attendance reports.

sentences.zh: 外諸孫成長，又於十宅外置百孫院。

translations.literal: As the outer grandsons grew up, outside the Ten Residences they also established the Hundred Grandsons' Court.
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial grandsons in the outer line grew up, the Hundred Grandsons' Court was established outside the Ten Residences.

sentences.zh: 每歲幸華清宮，宮側亦有十王院、百孫院。

translations.literal: Each year when the emperor visited Huaqing Palace, beside the palace there were also a Ten Princes' Court and a Hundred Grandsons' Court.
translations.idiomatic: Each year when the court visited Huaqing Palace, there were also a Ten Princes' Court and a Hundred Grandsons' Court beside the palace.

sentences.zh: 宮人每院四百，百孫院三四十人。

translations.literal: Palace women for each courtyard numbered four hundred; the Hundred Grandsons' Court thirty or forty persons.
translations.idiomatic: Each prince's courtyard had four hundred palace women assigned; the Hundred Grandsons' Court had thirty or forty.

sentences.zh: 又於宮中置維城庫，諸王月俸物，約之而給用。

translations.literal: Within the palace they also established the Weicheng storehouse. The princes' monthly stipends in goods were rationed and distributed for use.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace a Weicheng storehouse was also established. The princes' monthly stipends in goods were rationed and distributed from it.

sentences.zh: 諸孫納妃嫁女，亦就十宅中。

translations.literal: When grandsons took consorts or married daughters, this also took place within the Ten Residences.
translations.idiomatic: When grandsons took consorts or married off daughters, the ceremonies also took place within the Ten Residences.

sentences.zh: 太子不居於東宮，但居於乘輿所幸之別院。

translations.literal: The crown prince did not dwell in the Eastern Palace but only in the separate residence where the imperial carriage happened to favor.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince did not dwell in the Eastern Palace but only in whatever separate residence the emperor favored at the time.

sentences.zh: 太子亦分院而居，婚嫁則同親王、公主，在於崇仁之禮院。

translations.literal: The crown prince also dwelt in a separate courtyard. For marriage rites he was the same as imperial princes and princesses, at the ceremonial court in Chongren.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince also lived in a separate courtyard. For weddings he followed the same practice as imperial princes and princesses, at the ceremonial court in Chongren.

sentences.zh: 汴哀王璥，玄宗第三十子也，初名滔。

translations.literal: The Bian'ai Prince Jin was Emperor Xuanzong's thirtieth son; his original name was Tao.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian'ai Prince Jin was Xuanzong's thirtieth son. His birth name was Tao.

sentences.zh: 開元二十五年七月，封為汴王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan, 737, he was created Prince of Bian.

sentences.zh: 二十四年二月，改名璥，以其月薨。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-fourth year, his name was changed to Jin, and in that same month he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-fourth year, 736, his name was changed to Jin, and he died that same month.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：前史有云：「母愛者子抱」，太子瑛之廢，有由然矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The former histories have a saying: "Where the mother is loved, the son is embraced." The deposing of Crown Prince Ying had its reasons indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: The former histories say, "Where the mother is loved, the son is embraced." The deposing of Crown Prince Ying had its causes indeed.

sentences.zh: 琬為元帥，不幸遽薨，豈天啟亂階，何失眾望之速也！

translations.literal: Wan as supreme commander, unhappily died suddenly—was Heaven opening the steps of disorder? How swiftly he lost the hopes of the multitude!
translations.idiomatic: Wan as supreme commander died suddenly and untimely—was Heaven itself opening the way to disorder? How swiftly he lost the hopes of the realm!

sentences.zh: 永王璘，父在蜀城，兄居靈武，不能立忠孝之節，為社稷之謀，而乃聚兵江上，規為己利，不義不昵，以災其身，《書》所謂「自作孽，不可逭」也。

translations.literal: Prince of Yong Lin: his father was in the city of Shu, his elder brother dwelt at Lingwu. He could not establish the integrity of loyalty and filial piety or make plans for the altars of state, but instead gathered troops on the river and schemed profit for himself. Neither righteous nor intimate, he brought disaster upon himself—what the Documents calls "He who brings calamity upon himself cannot escape it."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yong, Lin: his father was in Shu, his elder brother at Lingwu. He could not uphold loyalty and filial piety or serve the altars of state, but instead gathered troops on the Yangzi and schemed for his own gain. Unrighteous and disloyal, he brought disaster upon himself—as the Documents say, "He who brings calamity upon himself cannot escape it."

sentences.zh: 豐王珙因緣厄運，竊有覬覦，不慎樞機，自貽伊咎，悲矣！

translations.literal: Prince of Feng Gong, taking advantage of misfortune's hour, secretly harbored covetous designs. He did not heed the pivot of power and brought calamity upon himself—lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Feng, Gong, seizing a moment of calamity, secretly harbored designs on the throne. He did not heed the pivot of power and brought ruin upon himself—lamentable indeed!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《螽斯》之詠，樂有子孫。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The ode "Zhongsi" rejoices in having sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: The ode "Zhongsi" rejoices in sons and grandsons.

sentences.zh: 用建籓屏，以崇本根。

translations.literal: They were used to establish the screen of the feudal domains and to exalt the root and trunk.
translations.idiomatic: They were made to establish the screen of the feudal domains and exalt the root of the house.

sentences.zh: 讒勝瑛廢，恩移至尊。

translations.literal: Slander prevailed and Ying was deposed; favor shifted to the sovereign's person.
translations.idiomatic: Slander prevailed and Ying was cast aside; favor shifted to the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 盜熾琬卒，情乖萬民。

translations.literal: Rebellion flared and Wan died; sentiment turned from the ten thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion flared and Wan died; the people's hopes were betrayed.

sentences.zh: 口禍豐珙，自災永璘。

translations.literal: Words brought calamity to Feng Gong; Yong Lin brought disaster on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Reckless words doomed Feng Gong; Yong Lin brought ruin on himself.

sentences.zh: 惜乎二胤，不如仁人。

translations.literal: Pity these two descendants—they were not like men of benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Pity these two princes—they were no match for men of virtue.
